svg.title: MarkeTech: the Docker Compose stack
svg.desc: Panel A: docker-compose.yml starts four containers. db (postgres:18-alpine) and redis (redis:8-alpine) are official images; backend and frontend are the images published on ghcr.io, or built from backend/Dockerfile and frontend/Dockerfile. db and redis are on the network internal (internal: true), backend on internal and web, frontend on web and the external network proxy, where a reverse proxy outside this repository reaches it in production. Only the frontend publishes a port, 127.0.0.1:8080 to 80. The volume db_data is mounted on /var/lib/postgresql, media on /app/media. Panel B: db and redis must pass their healthchecks before the backend starts and runs entrypoint.sh; the frontend starts after the backend. Panel C: Nginx serves the Vue build and passes /api, /_allauth, /admin, /static and /ws/ to backend:8000. Panel D: which container reads which variables of .env, and the variables set by the compose file itself.
svg.text: Four containers, three networks, two volumes. The same file runs on a development PC and in production. Follow the numbers 1 to 8.
Real files of the repository: docker-compose.yml, .env.example, both Dockerfiles, entrypoint.sh and nginx.conf (main, 30.10.2026).
docker compose up · services db, redis, backend, frontend
Configuration: .env and the environment set by the file

g.text: The network proxy is external: this file does not create it
It must exist before "docker compose up". In production, the reverse
proxy provides it. On a development PC, create it once by hand:
The reverse proxy is then simply absent: port 8080 is the way in.

svg.text: Docker network web: frontend and backend
Docker network internal (internal: true): backend, db, redis · no Internet in or out

g.text: The frontend never reaches the database, and the reverse proxy never reaches the backend
Each container is reached by the name of its service, inside the networks it shares: backend:8000, db, redis:6379. 8000, 5432 and 6379 are not
published on the machine. Docker keeps the volumes db_data and media when a container is removed or replaced by a new image.

g.text: Only the backend has an env_file
db: its three POSTGRES_ values, through "environment:" and ${...:?}.
frontend: only IMAGE_TAG, through Compose, in the tag of its image.
IMAGE_TAG: "latest" by default; "sha-" + 7 characters of a commit of main
pins one exact version of both images (rollback).
